acbl.name: ACBL
acbl.summary: Natural calls are not alerted and artificial calls are, apart from a list of exemptions such as Stayman, 4NT ace asks and a very strong 2♣. A few calls are announced instead: the 1NT opening range, a minor opening that may be short, transfers and other bids showing one named suit, and a forcing or semi-forcing 1NT response. A conventional call at 3NT or higher from opener's rebid on, and any control bid, gets a delayed alert after the auction; passes, doubles and redoubles are never delayed.

source.title: ACBL Alert Procedure
source.version: Effective February 16, 2026 (PDF titled "Alert Procedures Update February 2026"; supersedes April 15, 2024 and January 1, 2021 editions)

ebu.name: EBU
ebu.summary: The bidder's partner alerts any call that is not natural, or natural with a meaning the opponents would not expect. On the first round a fixed set of calls is announced instead, among them the 1NT range, short minors, natural two-level openings, Stayman and transfers. Above 3NT after the first round nothing is alerted except artificial first-round suit bids and some doubles and passes, and there is no delayed alert.

source.title: EBU Blue Book: EBU Player Handbook (chapter 4, Alerting and Announcing)
source.version: Revised 2024, effective 1 August 2024 (current edition per ebu.co.uk/blue-book as of Oct 2026)

wbf.name: WBF
wbf.summary: Artificial calls, and any call resting on a special partnership understanding, are alerted; natural calls are not. There are no announcements, no delayed alerts and no level cut-off, so conventional calls at the four level and above are alerted too. Non-forcing new-suit and jump-shift responses must be alerted, and behind screens each player alerts both their own calls and partner's.

source.title: WBF Alerting Policy
source.version: Adopted July 1997, revised August 2002 and August 2022; published by the WBF Systems Committee March 2023. Screen procedure from WBF General Conditions of Contest §16 and §33.2 (2022) and 'Using Bidding Boxes with Screens' §2.2 (February 2024)

alert.note: Asks for a four-card major. Exempt from alerting in the ACBL; the EBU announces it as "Stayman" and the WBF alerts it as artificial.
Stayman over 2NT, treated like 2♣ over 1NT: exempt in the ACBL, announced in the EBU. The WBF does not list it; it alerts every artificial call.
Denies a four-card major. Exempt in the ACBL and EBU; the WBF alerts it as artificial.
Natural major reply. The EBU alerts a 2♠ that does not deny four hearts.
Natural notrump rebid. The EBU alerts it when the 2♣ did not promise a major; the ACBL and WBF do not mention it and it reads as natural.
Transfer to the next suit up: partner names the suit ("Hearts", "Spades") in the ACBL and EBU. The WBF has no announcements and alerts it.
Transfer over a 2NT opening, announced like the 1NT ones. The WBF alerts it as artificial.
Plain completion of the transfer. The WBF alerts it as a call resting on a partnership understanding.
Super-accept: a jump completion promising four-card support. The EBU and WBF alert the specific holding; the ACBL does not mention it and it reads as a natural raise.

alert.when: responder's rebid has an agreed artificial meaning
alert.note: Alerted only when responder's rebid carries an agreed artificial meaning (for example a game force with long spades); a natural second suit is not.
Four-level transfer to a major, announced by naming the suit even above 3NT. The WBF alerts it as artificial.
Completion of the transfer. The WBF alerts it as a call based on an understanding.
Shows four cards in the major bid and five in the other.
Natural choice of game. The WBF does not mention it; natural calls are not alerted there.
Puppet Stayman over 1NT. The ACBL exempts any major-suit ask over notrump; the EBU alerts Puppet rather than announcing it, and the WBF alerts it as artificial.
Asks for a four- or five-card major. Exempt in the ACBL as a major-suit ask; alerted in the EBU and WBF.
Shows at least one four-card major and no five-card major.
Shows a five-card major. The ACBL lists it as a natural reply that is still alerted; the EBU treats it as natural, and the WBF does not mention it.
Natural: no four- or five-card major.
Responder bids the major he does not hold. The ACBL treats it as a one-suit showing call to announce (uncertain: some directors want an alert); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Shows both majors. The EBU does not alert it because it is above 3NT after the first round.
Relay forcing opener to bid 3♣.
Forced completion of the relay.
Stayman-like cuebid, with the route showing or denying a stopper. The ACBL exempts bids in the overcaller's suit after a notrump opening; the EBU and WBF alert it.
To play, but its route shows or denies a stopper. The ACBL treats it as natural; the EBU alerts the stopper message, and the WBF's rule for special understandings points the same way.
Stayman that may be weak. Still exempt in the ACBL and still announced "Stayman" in the EBU; the WBF alerts it as artificial.
Passing opener's reply is natural.

alert.when: playing crawling Stayman (2♥ shows both majors, weak)
alert.note: Crawling variant: weak with both majors. The ACBL alerts it; the EBU and WBF do not mention it, but its extra message is alertable under their general rules.
Natural game-forcing new suit (2♥ only over 1♠). The EBU announces it as "natural, game-forcing"; the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.

alert.when: the 2♣ response may hold fewer than three clubs
alert.note: Alerted when the 2♣ response may hold fewer than three clubs, since it is then not natural.
Artificial game-forcing raise.
Shows shortness in the suit bid.
Shows extras without shortness. The ACBL reads it as natural; the EBU and WBF alert it as a coded strength message.
Coded hand description, not an offer to play. The ACBL gives a delayed alert because it is at 3NT on opener's rebid.
Shows a good second suit. Natural in the ACBL and above 3NT after the first round in the EBU; the WBF alerts the reply.
Minimum sign-off. The WBF does not list it separately; it reads as natural.
Artificial game-forcing raise.
Step replies showing strength or controls.
Step reply at 3NT. The ACBL delays the alert to the end of the auction.
Step reply above 3NT. The ACBL gives a delayed alert, the EBU none after the first round; the WBF has no level cut-off.
Responder's artificial follow-up asks (ACBL uncertain: depends on the scheme, and those at 3NT or above are delayed).
Artificial raises showing four-card support.
Preemptive jump raise, alerted in the ACBL and EBU when the next hand passed. The WBF does not list it and reads a jump raise as natural (uncertain).
Artificial re-ask or game try after the artificial raise.
Jump raise weaker than a limit raise; the ACBL does not alert it after a double. The WBF reads it as a natural raise (uncertain).
A mixed raise shown by an artificial bid (such as 3♣). The ACBL does not alert a jump cuebid after an overcall.
Double jump showing shortness. Alerted at once even at the four level, as responder's first call.
Opener's jump showing shortness below 3NT.
Opener's splinter above 3NT. The ACBL delays the alert; the EBU does not alert it after the first round; the WBF alerts it.
Artificial raise by a passed hand.
Artificial reply about opener's strength.
Return to the major. Natural in the ACBL and EBU; the WBF alerts opener's replies as artificial (it groups them, so this is our reading).
Artificial raise by a passed hand.
Artificial: a full opening with game interest.
Sign-off showing a light opening. Natural in the ACBL and EBU; the WBF alerts it as a step reply.
Partner announces "Semi-forcing" in the ACBL and the upper limit ("Up to 12") in the EBU. The WBF alerts it as a special understanding (uncertain).
Not announced in the ACBL after a third- or fourth-seat opening. The EBU has no seat rule, so the announcement still applies; the WBF alerts it (uncertain).
Rebid in a three-card minor: natural in the ACBL and EBU. The WBF alerts a rebid that may be that short.

alert.when: opener's minor may be a doubleton
alert.note: Rebid in a minor that may be a doubleton is not natural (EBU uncertain).
Partner announces "Forcing" (ACBL: add "could have four spades" if 1♠ may be bypassed). The WBF alerts it as a special understanding (uncertain).
Not announced in the ACBL after a third- or fourth-seat opening. The EBU has no seat rule, so it still announces; the WBF alerts it (uncertain).
Rebid in a three-card minor: natural in the ACBL and EBU. The WBF alerts a rebid that may be that short.

alert.when: opener's minor may be a doubleton
alert.note: Rebid in a minor that may be a doubleton is not natural (EBU uncertain).
Strong, forcing single raise.
Weak jump raise, alerted when the next hand passed (WBF uncertain).
Opener's bid showing a stopper rather than length. Listed by the EBU; the ACBL and WBF alert artificial calls below 3NT.
Natural four-card major response.
Natural, but denies a four-card major unless strong. The ACBL and EBU (uncertain) leave the inference to questions; the WBF alerts it as a special understanding (uncertain).
Natural rebid that may bypass a major.
Transfer: partner names the suit shown ("Hearts", "Spades"). The WBF alerts it.
Denies a four-card major. Alerted in the ACBL and WBF; the EBU announces "No major".
Accepting the transfer. Natural in the ACBL (uncertain) and EBU unless it promises a holding; the WBF alerts it.
Artificial strong opening. The ACBL exempts a very strong 2♣ (alert one that may be merely strong); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Waiting or negative reply. Exempt in the ACBL; alerted in the EBU and WBF.
Natural positive reply.
Natural balanced rebid.
Natural weak two. The EBU announces the strength ("Weak"); the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.

alert.when: a new-suit response is not forcing
alert.note: Alerted when a new-suit response is not forcing. The EBU and WBF do not cover it directly; an unexpected meaning is alertable under both.

alert.when: a raise is invitational or forcing, not preemptive
alert.note: Alerted in the ACBL when a raise is not preemptive. The EBU and WBF do not cover it; this follows the ACBL.
Natural weak two. The EBU announces the strength ("Weak"); the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.

alert.when: a new-suit response is not forcing
alert.note: Alerted when a new-suit response is not forcing. The EBU and WBF do not cover it directly; an unexpected meaning is alertable under both.

alert.when: a raise is invitational or forcing, not preemptive
alert.note: Alerted in the ACBL when a raise is not preemptive. The EBU and WBF do not cover it; this follows the ACBL.
Natural weak two. The EBU announces the strength ("Weak"); the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.

alert.when: a new-suit response is not forcing
alert.note: Alerted when a new-suit response is not forcing. The EBU and WBF do not cover it directly; an unexpected meaning is alertable under both.

alert.when: a raise is invitational or forcing, not preemptive
alert.note: Alerted in the ACBL when a raise is not preemptive. The EBU and WBF do not cover it; this follows the ACBL.
Asking bid. The ACBL exempts any forcing 2NT over a two-level preempt; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Coded replies about strength and suit quality.
Coded reply (such as a solid suit). The ACBL delays the alert as a 3NT call on opener's rebid.
Weak two in an unknown major or other options; also pre-alerted in the ACBL.
Pass-or-correct response (ACBL uncertain).
Enquiry. The ACBL exempts a forcing 2NT over a two-level preempt (uncertain, as Multi may hold strong hands); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Coded replies to the enquiry.
Three-suited opening.
Asks for the short suit; not a preempt, so the ACBL 2NT exemption does not apply.
Show the short suit.
Pass-or-correct response. Listed by the EBU; the ACBL and WBF alert a call that does not promise the suit.
Two-suiter in the majors.
Natural choice of major.
Asking bid; the ACBL 2NT exemption covers only weak preempts.
Relay: hearts or a big balanced hand.
Forced relay.
Balanced, stronger than a direct 2NT. The EBU alerts the unexpected strength; the ACBL treats it as natural, and the WBF does not mention it.
Natural heart rebid after the relay (EBU uncertain).
Very weak reply, says nothing about hearts.
Relay to 3♣. The ACBL exempts a forcing 2NT after a two-level preempt (uncertain); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Forced reply to the relay.
Lead-directing, with support for partner, not a suit to play.
Ace or keycard ask. Exempt in the ACBL and above 3NT in the EBU; the WBF has no level cut-off.
Replies to the ask. The ACBL gives a delayed alert; the EBU does not alert above 3NT; the WBF alerts them.
King ask and its replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Ace or keycard ask. Exempt in the ACBL and above 3NT in the EBU; the WBF has no level cut-off.
Replies to the ask. The ACBL gives a delayed alert; the EBU does not alert above 3NT; the WBF alerts them.
King ask and its replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Ace or keycard ask. Exempt in the ACBL and above 3NT in the EBU; the WBF has no level cut-off.
Replies to the ask. The ACBL gives a delayed alert; the EBU does not alert above 3NT; the WBF alerts them.
King ask and its replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Asks for the trump queen. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted above 3NT in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Show or deny the queen (and kings). Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Ace ask directly over notrump. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU alerts it as an artificial first-round suit bid above 3NT, and the WBF alerts it.
Ace replies. Delayed in the ACBL (opener's rebid), not alerted above 3NT in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
King ask and replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Gerber outside a direct notrump auction. Not exempt in the ACBL, so delayed; not alerted in the EBU; alerted in the WBF.
Keycard ask. Delayed in the ACBL; the EBU does not alert it after the first round; the WBF alerts it.
Keycard step replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Keycard ask in the agreed minor. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted above 3NT in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Keycard step replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Keycard ask excluding the void. Delayed in the ACBL; the EBU alerts it only as a first-round jump; the WBF alerts it.
Keycard replies ignoring that suit. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Asks partner to choose a slam, not a notrump offer. Delayed in the ACBL; not alerted in the EBU; alerted in the WBF.
Natural choice of strain.
Asks for a stopper for 3NT. The ACBL exempts cuebids after an opening and overcall; the EBU (below 3NT or on the first round) and WBF alert it.
Asks for a stopper in a suit the partnership has bid (ACBL uncertain; delayed at 3NT or above after opener's rebid).
The ACBL always delays control bids, even below 3NT; the EBU and WBF alert them at once.
Trump-quality asks and step replies (ACBL uncertain).

alert.call: Asks, replies and control bids above 3NT
alert.note: Delayed in the ACBL; the EBU does not alert above 3NT after the first round; the WBF alerts them.
Shows or denies slam interest rather than offering to play. The ACBL delays the alert; the EBU (3NT is not above 3NT) and WBF alert it at once.
The ACBL delays all control bids; the EBU does not alert above 3NT; the WBF alerts them.
Takeout double of a natural suit opening. The WBF has no explicit exemption but treats it as generally understood (uncertain).

alert.when: the double of 1NT is not for penalty
alert.note: Takeout or conventional double of a 1NT opening. Listed by the EBU; the ACBL and WBF alert a double of notrump that is not for penalty or values.
Negative double. Exempt in the ACBL (announce the major if it usually holds five); the EBU announces it when it shows just four of the other major; the WBF alerts it (uncertain).
Negative double after other one-level openings. The WBF alerts a double that is not for penalty (uncertain).
Negative double after a preempt. The ACBL exempts only a penalty double here; the EBU does not alert a takeout-style double; the WBF alerts it.
Negative, penalty or card-showing double after a notrump opening. Exempt in the ACBL and not alerted in the EBU; the WBF alerts a non-penalty double.
Takeout double by advancer after they raise. Not alerted in the ACBL or EBU; the WBF alerts it as a special understanding.
Shows exactly three-card support. The ACBL exempts all doubles from opener's rebid on; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Support redouble. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Cuebid showing both majors. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU (overcalls are never announced) and WBF alert it.
Cuebid showing the other major and a minor. Exempt in the ACBL; alerted in the EBU and WBF.

alert.when: the cuebid shows a pair of suits other than the usual one
alert.note: A cuebid showing a non-standard pair of suits.
Asks for overcaller's minor.
Two lowest unbid suits. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU and WBF alert it as two-suited.

alert.when: 2NT shows suits other than the two lowest unbid
alert.note: A 2NT overcall showing two suits other than the lowest two.
Two-suited 2NT after an opening and a response; exempt in the ACBL since 2026. The EBU and WBF do not list it; both alert a two-suited 2NT.
Shows a one-suiter.
The suit bid plus a higher one.
Natural spade one-suiter.
Relay or pass-or-correct bid.
Limit raise or better. Exempt in the ACBL after an opening and overcall; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Raise of the overcall, limit or better. Exempt in the ACBL; alerted in the EBU, and by the WBF's rule for artificial calls.
Double of an artificial bid asking for that suit. Not alerted in the ACBL or EBU; the WBF alerts it.
Double of an artificial bid asking for a different lead or against that suit.
Lead-directing double such as Lightner. The ACBL does not alert doubles of 3NT or higher; the EBU alerts the lead message even above 3NT, and so does the WBF's special-meaning rule.
Relay to 3♣ (ACBL uncertain: its forcing-2NT exemption may reach advancer).
Forced completion of the relay.
Artificial cuebid by advancer (ACBL uncertain); not listed by the EBU or WBF, but artificial.
Shows the two unbid suits, not a notrump hand.
Shows the fourth suit with tolerance for partner. The ACBL announces the suit (uncertain); the EBU (uncertain) and WBF alert it.
Game try, not penalty. The ACBL exempts all doubles from opener's rebid on; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Cuebids of the shown suits. Exempt in the ACBL as raises or good hands; the EBU and WBF alert them.
Shows values or penalty interest. Exempt in the ACBL and not listed by the EBU (uncertain); the WBF alerts it.
Natural and non-forcing. The ACBL and WBF alert a non-forcing new suit by an unpassed hand; the EBU's "natural, non-forcing" announcement fits it.
The minor plus the other major; a direct overcall, so not delayed.
Cuebid of the weak two. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU (first-round artificial bid) and WBF alert it.
Two-suited jump over a weak 2♦. The ACBL does not mention it; it alerts natural bids that also show another suit.
Artificial and forcing (one round); does not promise the suit.
Natural rebids: raise, notrump with a stopper, preference.
Artificial and forcing (game force); does not promise the suit.
Natural rebids: raise, notrump with a stopper, preference.
Natural try promising three or more cards in the suit (WBF uncertain).

alert.when: the try may be a doubleton or shorter
alert.note: A try that may be a doubleton or shorter.
Natural; the extra strength is standard.
Artificial forcing enquiry.
Natural replies; an artificial reply is alerted.
Relay to 2♦.
Artificial game force.
Forced completion of the relay.
Relay to 2♦ (also after a 1NT rebid).
Artificial game force.
Forced completion of the relay.
Asks partner to pick another suit. Exempt in the ACBL in the balancing seat or after a balancing double; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Asks partner to pick another suit.
Artificial relay or enquiry, not a natural notrump.
Forced or coded reply to the relay.
Partner states the range ("15 to 17") in the ACBL and EBU. The WBF does not alert a natural notrump opening of any range.
Natural; only the 1NT range is announced.
Partner announces the minimum length ("Could be two"). The WBF has no rule for it but alerts a 1♣ that may be short (uncertain).
Partner announces the minimum length. The WBF alerts a 1♦ that can hold fewer than three cards as artificial.
Strong, forcing, artificial 1♣; the ACBL also wants a pre-alert.
When 2♣ is natural. The ACBL alerts any natural 2♣; the EBU announces its strength band; the WBF does not alert a natural opening.
A natural two-level opening that may hold 12+ HCP (not 4th seat). The ACBL alerts it; the EBU announces the band ("Intermediate"); the WBF does not cover it, and natural openings are not alerted.
Based on a long running suit, not a natural notrump. The WBF does not list it; it is not natural, so it is alerted.
Transfer to a major. The ACBL announces the suit shown (and wants a pre-alert); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Natural 1NT overcall in the usual range.
Alerted in the ACBL below 14 HCP and in the EBU when well under 15. The WBF does not cover it; this follows the ACBL.
A weak jump overcall is natural and expected, treated like a weak two opening: no regulator alerts it.

alert.when: jump overcalls are intermediate or strong, not weak
alert.note: Natural but not weak, so not what opponents expect: the ACBL and the EBU alert it; the WBF does not cover it, so this follows the ACBL.
A natural cuebid of a natural one-level opening. The ACBL alerts it; the EBU and WBF do not list it, but a natural cuebid is unexpected.
Invitational double raise: natural and expected.
Preemptive jump raise, alerted in the ACBL and EBU when the next hand passed. The WBF reads a raise as natural (uncertain).

A weak jump shift by responder with no interference. Strong is the default, so the ACBL and the WBF alert the weak version; the EBU announces it as natural and non-forcing. Not to be read as a preempt like a weak two or a weak jump overcall.
After a double or an overcall the weak jump shift is standard: no alert in the ACBL, and none in the EBU (uncertain). The WBF alerts every non-forcing jump shift.
Natural and forcing. The EBU announces "natural, game-forcing"; the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.
Shows a control in the suit bid. The ACBL always delays it; the EBU does not alert it above 3NT after the first round (it does below); the WBF alerts it.
